metadata.title: Predicting teachers’ research reading: A machine learning approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the 2018 PISA language teacher questionnaire and restricts the analytic sample to teachers with available information on the selected personal, educational, instructional, and professional variables (final N=10,469). The authors state that the language teacher questionnaire does not require preprocessing for setting appropriate weighting, unlike some other PISA questionnaires, implying that standard PISA weighting procedures are available in the underlying dataset. However, the manuscript does not explicitly report whether complex survey weights (and which weight variable) were applied in the logistic regression and SVM training/evaluation. Because the models are ML classifiers and the paper does not describe weight-aware estimation, the safest interpretation is that the analysis may be unweighted or that weighting is not discussed; this limits the extent to which results can be interpreted as population-representative across the 18 included countries.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable is a dichotomized self-reported reading-time category (light vs heavy readers) derived from a Likert item, not a cognitive achievement score with PISA plausible values. Therefore, plausible values are not applicable to the outcome modeled. The paper also does not describe an explicit missing-data strategy for the 10,469 analytic sample (e.g., listwise deletion or imputation), which is a reporting gap because missingness can vary by country and by which questionnaire items are available.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: From the 107,367 teachers who completed the PISA 2018 language teacher questionnaire, the authors included only 10,469 teachers for whom the required personal, educational, instructional, and professional variables were available for the study. The subset covers 18 countries (Albania; Azerbaijan—Baku City only; Brazil; Chile; Chinese Taipei; Dominican Republic; Germany; Hong Kong; Macao; Malaysia; Morocco; Panama; Portugal; Republic of Korea; Spain; United Arab Emirates; United Kingdom; United States) and excludes Peru due to insufficient availability of variables for the analysis. The outcome was recoded from a 4-point self-report into two categories (light readers: <3 hours/week; heavy readers: >6 hours/week), and features were scaled using RobustScaler; additionally, correlated features were reduced to avoid multicollinearity (e.g., experience removed in favor of age).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Language teacher questionnaire (2018), teacher professional reading time (light vs heavy)
main_findings.target_variable: Professional reading time category (light vs heavy)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Logistic regression (hold-out) Accuracy: 0.64; Precision (macro/weighted): 0.64/0.64; Recall (macro/weighted): 0.63/0.64; F1 (macro/weighted): 0.63/0.64. SVM (hold-out) Accuracy: 0.65; Precision (macro/weighted): 0.64/0.64; Recall (macro/weighted): 0.63/0.65; F1 (macro/weighted): 0.64/0.64. ROC AUC (both models): 0.70. Confusion-matrix totals: 2,094 cases; SVM correct for light readers 481 vs 471 for logistic regression; SVM F1 for light readers ~0.57 vs ~0.56 for logistic regression.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 language teacher questionnaire the study leveraged teaching reading comprehension strategies, length of reading assignment, general book reading habits, general news reading habits, and age to classify professional reading time (light vs heavy), finding that both logistic regression and SVM achieved very similar performance with hold-out accuracy around 0.64–0.65 and ROC AUC of 0.70. This indicates that classroom reading instruction practices and the amount/type of reading teachers assign are strongly associated with teachers’ professional research reading time, suggesting that teacher development policies should support reading-strategy instruction and reading engagement as part of research literacy initiatives, while noting that the study is predictive (not causal) and does not report a missing-data strategy or explicit survey-weight use.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses the 2018 PISA language teacher questionnaire and analyzes a restricted cross-country subset of 18 countries (final analytic sample N=10,469 teachers) to predict whether teachers are “light” vs “heavy” professional readers based on self-reported weekly reading time. The outcome is dichotomized (<3 hours/week vs >6 hours/week), and features are scaled with RobustScaler; correlated predictors were reduced to mitigate multicollinearity. Two ML classifiers—logistic regression and SVM—were trained using a 5:1 train/test split with 10-fold cross-validation on the training set for hyperparameter tuning. On the hold-out set, accuracy was 0.64 (logistic regression) vs 0.65 (SVM), with ROC AUC of 0.70 for both; precision/recall/F1 were also very similar. The most important predictors in logistic regression were teaching reading comprehension strategies, the length of reading assignments, and teachers’ general reading habits (books and news), with age also contributing. Limitations include modest predictive performance, lack of an explicit missing-data handling description, and no clear reporting on whether PISA complex survey weights were applied; therefore, results should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.
